A `gate.py control` fires its whole `[[gate]]` entry with the guard removed, and nextest's default fail-fast ends that
firing at its first red. So an older case touching the same code can carry the red while the guard's own new case is
never run, and the control still reads `holds`. Before a control counts as witnessing a new case, read the removed
firing's log for that case's own FAIL line. Where it is absent, give that case a control of its own whose entry
selects it alone. This extends testing.md's remove-the-guard entry (2026-09-25), which stands at its size cap.
Extended 2026-11-16: the entry's whole set must also END with the guard removed — an older test whose waiter runs
inside `std::thread::scope` with no deadline of its own hangs after it panics (the scope joins that waiter), so a
control on a whole-module entry reads `timeout` however every guard case fails; fire the control on an entry filtered
to the guard's own cases, and give it `--timeout`, whose default bound waits out each hanging firing.

The session documented and pinned the wake condition of viola wait: every turn-ended record wakes a parked wait whatever its background_tasks count (zero, one, three, null, and a booted held turn with 2), and an activity record or a harness-origin prompt-submitted after a task-free turn end never wakes it.
No product code moved: no command, IPC method, event kind, field, output line, refusal, exit code or env var is added or changed; the wake set stays six kinds; the MCP wait tool is unchanged.
The change is test-only: new unit and booted CLI wait tests, a new fake-agent script for a held turn, and a bound on the unit tests' park waits.
The stamped-home test fixture now takes one viola verify stamp per built test binary under a lock and copies it into each test's fresh home, never a link; two new verify-suite tests pin that copies share no file and reuse one stamp.
Measured: the stamped-home class runs under the unchanged 20 s ci kill (rest max 10.9 s, verify-window max 43.4 s under its own 60 s kill), the class wall fell 56.1 to 48.4 s, and the carried CI timing red closed green 7 of 7 checks.
Carried, not fixed: two older wait unit tests still hang past a failure; owner the route entry Version done-check. Nothing is retired.

The session is test-only. It pins the wait wake condition: every turn-ended record wakes a parked wait, whatever its background_tasks (unit cases 0, 1, 3 and null, and a booted case with 2), and activity and a harness-origin prompt-submitted after a task-free turn end never wake it.

The stamped-home test fixture now takes one viola verify stamp per built binary, under a lock, at target/e2e-home/viola-stamp-<key16>/home. It copies that stamp into each test's home, never as a link. The stamp dir has no owner record, and another build's stamp is swept only when its lock is free.
Measured: the stamped-home class wall went from 56.069 to 48.381 s (321 tests on both sides), with rest max 10.913 s under the unchanged 20 s ci kill and window max 43.358 s under its 60 s kill. The carried CI timing red is closed (CI green 7/7).

body_fields.because: The chunk pins that the wake rule reads only the event kind, so a held turn end with background tasks wakes a parked wait and activity or a harness turn never does, and no row of the cli surface states when `wait` returns.

body:
The session documented and pinned the wait wake condition with tests only: every turn-ended record wakes a parked wait whatever its background_tasks count (zero, one, three, null, and a booted case with two), and the activity record and a harness-origin prompt-submitted after a task-free turn end never wake it.
No product symbol, channel method, MCP tool, event kind, field, env var or socket was added or changed; the wake set stays six kinds and the wake rule reads only the event kind.
The stamped-home test fixture now takes one viola verify stamp per built binary, under an exclusive lock on its lock sibling, and copies it into each test's home, never a link; the stamp dir carries no owner record, and other builds' stamps are swept only when their lock is taken with try_lock.
A new fake-agent script with synthetic text only drives a held turn end; the CI per-test kill is unchanged, and the carried CI timing red closed green on measurement.
viola carries no scheduled-wake count beside background_tasks; carrying session_crons as a count is a founder candidate, not taken, and the driver-side fix for a re-parking waiter landed outside viola.

body_fields.what: the CLI wait verb's park-and-wake logic; edited in its test module only (a park bound on the tests' waits and two wake-rule unit tests), its product code unchanged
a new fake-agent script fixture (fake-script.v1) of synthetic hook steps for a held turn end, a notification and a harness-origin turn; replaced nothing, added new
the end-to-end tests of the wait and last verbs against a fake-agent instance; edited to add the booted held-turn and no-false-wake cases

the test-support stamped-home fixture that gives each test its own viola home from a viola verify stamp; edited so one stamp per built binary is taken under a lock, copied per test, and other builds' stamps swept
the end-to-end tests of viola verify and its stamps; edited to add tests that stamped-home copies share no file with the stamp or each other and that one stamp serves every home
the test runner's CI profile with the per-test kill for verify-driven tests; edited in a comment only, no kill, filter or period moved

body: The wait method of the wrapper channel and the MCP wait tool: the wake condition is now pinned by tests (every turn end wakes whatever its background_tasks; activity and a harness-origin prompt-submitted do not); a row stating which records wake or do not wake a parked wait may need the harness-origin prompt-submitted named.

The decision that a Stop hook's background tasks cross only as a count: the count still crosses alone and no scheduled-wake count crosses beside it; a session_crons count stands as a founder candidate, a boundary widening not taken.

The decision that only viola verify writes the stamps file, and that stamps are checked before and under lock: test homes now copy one verify-taken stamp per built binary under an exclusive lock; verify is still the sole writer, the copy is no write of a stamp.
The decision that tests use their own home: each test's home is now a copy of a shared per-binary stamp, never a link, and the copies share no file with the stamp or each other.

The rules that test-side removal touches only dirs the tests created, the e2e-home linked-base guard and its keepers, and that viola never touches the e2e-home backing: the fixture now sweeps other builds' stamp dirs under the e2e-home base, each only when its lock is taken with try_lock.
The decision that test homes are kept out of git: the stamp dirs live under the build target's e2e-home tree.

The recorded-fixture hygiene rules (fixtures reviewed before commit, viola-format fixtures under the hygiene walk, recordings scrubbed or refused): a new fake-agent script fixture was added, synthetic text only, no recorded fixture.
The rule that test seams live only under the fake-agent feature: the new cases drive the fake agent by a scripted held turn end, no new seam added.
The harness-prefix literals that mark a harness-origin prompt-submitted: such a turn after a task-free end is now pinned as non-waking for wait.

The rule that driver policy sits outside viola (mechanism, not policy): telling a finished turn from a paused one is the driver's, and the re-parking fix was made in the driver's own waiter, not in viola.
The SHA-256 content-hash rows: the test-side stamp key is a SHA-256 over the built viola and fake-agent binaries, a test-support use, not the pinned-copy key.

body_fields.fact: A turn end carries no scheduled-wake count; background_tasks is the only count that crosses, and carrying session_crons as a second count is a boundary widening left to the founder.

Each stamped test home is a copy of one viola verify stamp per built binary, taken under an exclusive lock, never a link, sharing no file with the stamp or other homes; the stamp dir carries no owner record.
The test fixture sweeps another build's stamp dir under the e2e-home base only when it takes that stamp's lock with try_lock, never a stamp a running build holds.

The session documented and pinned the wait wake condition with tests alone: no product symbol, IPC method, event kind, data key, env var or socket changed, and the wake set stays 6 kinds.
It pinned that every turn-ended wakes a parked wait whatever its background_tasks (unit cases zero, one, three and null, and a booted case holding 2 tasks with a closing question), and that no false wake comes from the Notification activity or a harness-origin prompt-submitted after a task-free turn end.
It added a fake agent turn script with five gated steps (a held turn end, a default stop, a notification, a harness-injected prompt, a default stop), synthetic text only.
It changed the stamped-home fixture: one viola verify stamp per built binary, taken once under an exclusive lock and copied into each test's home, never linked; the stamp dir carries no owner record and another build's stamp is swept only when its lock is free.
It measured the stamped-home class under the unchanged ci kills: rest max 10.913 s under the 20 s kill, verify_window_ max 43.358 s under the 60 s kill, 321 tests on both sides, class wall 56.069 to 48.381 s; CI read green 7 of 7 and the carried CI timing red closed.
Nothing retired; a carry stands: two older wait unit tests still hang past a failure under a clock that never moves, owned by a later route entry.

a fake agent turn script (fake-script format, gated steps) driving a held turn end with background tasks, then a notification and a harness-injected turn; new

the viola wait and viola last E2E suite, the CLI run as a subprocess over the fake agent; edited with two booted path3 wait cases (wake on a turn end holding background tasks, no false wake after a task-free end)

the shared test helper holding the stamped-home rstest fixture chain and the per-test home under target/e2e-home; edited so each home copies one verify stamp per built binary, taken under a lock, with the sweep of other builds' stamps
the viola verify integration suite; edited with two root tests that stamped-home copies share no file with the stamp or each other and that one stamp serves every home
the nextest configuration holding the test layer filtersets and the per-test kill lines of the ci profile; edited in the verify-driven override's comment only, no kill, filter or period moved

body: contract/viola-wait/non-waking-records: the activity and wheel records row does not name the harness-origin prompt-submitted nor the Notification activity after a task-free turn end; both are now pinned non-waking by a booted case and a unit test.

contract/viola-wait/wake, contract/viola-wait/turn-ended, contract/wait/wake-kinds and contract/channel-wait/wake-kinds: the wake set is unchanged at 6 kinds, but every turn-ended now provably wakes whatever its background_tasks (0, 1, 3, null, and 2 booted); a row restating the wake set may want that clause.

decision/verify-sole-stamp-writer, decision/stamps-written-only-by-verify, decision/stamps-only-from-verify, decision/stamps-from-fake-agent-verify, decision/fake-agent-replay-for-stamps, decision/single-writer-state-files and decision/single-writers: the stamp is still taken only through viola verify against the fake agent; the copy into a home writes no stamp.

decision/verify-window-60s-kill: the 60 s kill for the verify_window_ class holds unchanged; measured max 43.358 s.

decision/test-home-owner-record-sweep, decision/owner-record-removed-last, decision/e2e-homes-under-one-root, decision/e2e-homes-under-target-e2e-home and decision/e2e-home-base-checks: a new stamp dir lives under target/e2e-home with no owner record, and stamps of other builds are swept only when their lock is taken; the owner-record sweep rule may want that exception.

decision/bounded-remove-the-guard-witness: a remove-the-guard control on a park test needs a bounded park wait and an entry that runs only the guard's cases; a waiter with no deadline hangs the entry past the bound (120 s timeout against 2.21 s on the filtered entry).

decision/injected-clock, decision/test-clocks-behind-clock-seam and decision/zero-flakiness: two older wait unit tests still hang past a failure, joining a waiter parked on a huge timeout under an injected clock that never moves; a carry, not fixed.
contract/fake-script/format and contract/fake-script/gated-step: a new committed script uses five gated steps across Stop, Notification and UserPromptSubmit.
decision/synthetic-fixture-text, decision/scrubbed-fixtures and decision/fixtures-never-from-real-prompts: the new fake agent script carries synthetic text only.

decision/harness-turn-keeps-the-wheel, decision/injected-turn-keeps-wheel, contract/prompt-submitted/origin-harness and contract/events/harness-prompt: a harness-origin prompt-submitted is now also pinned as never waking a parked wait.
decision/e2e-for-critical-paths, decision/e2e-over-fake-agent and decision/cli-tests-as-subprocess: path3 gains two booted wait cases over the fake agent.
decision/cli-mcp-identical-payloads and contract/mcp-cli-parity/refusal: MCP wait holds by construction, its code untouched; the parity witness ran in pre-push.
decision/shared-e2e-helpers and decision/one-shared-test-helper: the stamp, copy-tree and file-hash helpers were added once to the shared test support, not copied.
decision/no-shared-mutable-state and decision/tests-run-in-parallel: one stamp is shared across parallel tests behind an exclusive lock, and the copies share no file with it or each other.
decision/test-layer-filtersets and decision/os-gated-cases-in-binary-root: the two stamp tests sit at the verify suite's root because a test(=name) filter matches no test inside a module.

body_fields.fact: A turn-ended wakes a parked viola wait whatever its background_tasks (zero, any count, or null); telling a finished session from a paused one is the driver's, and viola carries no scheduled-wake count.

Stamped test homes copy one viola verify stamp per pair of built binaries, kept under target/e2e-home as viola-stamp-<key16>/home keyed by the binaries' hashes and taken under an exclusive lock on its .lock sibling.
The stamp dir carries no owner record; another build's stamp is swept only when its lock is taken without waiting.
Each stamped home is a copy of the stamp, never a link: no file is shared between the stamp and any home, or between two homes.
